topic: Local LLMs reproduce Claude: what the experiments show
title: Local LLMs reproduce Claude? What the receipts show
description: Working description; the package stage overwrites this. A developer ran the Claude-at-home experiment and published the numbers: what actually got reproduced, at what speed, and what it costs.
hook_candidates: Claude at home, free? The receipts say slower
You want Claude at home. One man tested it.
Everyone says local AI matches Claude now
Your subscription isn't the target. The claim is.
Sixty to eighty tokens a second. His box does thirty.
A secondhand graphics card reproduced Claude. Half of it.
He reproduced last year's Claude in his bedroom
The keyword in his verdict is almost
What got reproduced isn't what you think
narration_full: You pay for Claude every month. Then a post says you could run it at home for free. One developer actually tried it. His box is a home P C, two generations old, with a secondhand graphics card. It runs local models, A I stored as files on his own machine. His test was one hard job he built himself: rebuild a research simulation as working code. On that job, the local models landed very close to Claude Sonnet. So what did he measure? Claude's app usually streams sixty to eighty tokens a second, tokens being the little chunks of words it writes. His big local models? Thirty tokens a second. He says he's happy to get it. That's just under half the speed of a subscription. So how does a giant model fit on a gaming card? Quantization, storing the model's numbers with fewer bits, shrinks the file until it fits in your card's memory. The other trick is mixture of experts, waking only a few specialist parts per token. A huge model ends up running at small-model speed. Now the verdict he wrote. His best local models edge past last year's Claude and almost tie today's Sonnet. The keyword, he writes, is almost. No blind test, no head-to-head benchmark, and no drop-in replacement for the top Claude. In another engineer's test, a leaderboard favorite did nothing while a plainer model finished. Think of a local model as a cover band that has rehearsed your setlist. On the songs it knows, it sounds like the record. His simulation job was one of those songs. Shout a request it never learned, and it fumbles. So Claude at home is real, and it's a trade, not a replacement. Even the man who ran it still pays ten dollars a month for the original.

analogy.vehicle: a cover band that has rehearsed your setlist
analogy.mapping: the local model is the band, the original recording is Claude; on the tasks you repeat every week it is hard to tell them apart
analogy.limit: a request it never learned, a room too big (context past what it holds), or release-day speed breaks the picture
